_about: scholar-visual flat-file corpus (Backend B). agentic-vision MCP is NOT connected in this session, so cards live here. Card schema is scholar-visual Section 4. Captured images are INTERNAL RESEARCH REFERENCE ONLY (Section 9) - they inform direction, they are not assets to ship, reproduce, or republish.
_staleness_note: The normal staleness policy assumes a live product whose UI drifts. It does not apply the same way here: the subject is Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010), a shipped and frozen build. The artefact these cards describe cannot change. What CAN be wrong is the wiki editor's extraction, not the game. So freshness is tracked against the upload date only as a proxy for extraction quality, never as 'this may no longer reflect the game'.
_capture_method: Screen capture through the claude-in-chrome browser tier of image pages legitimately rendered in the browser. Each corpus file is therefore a JPEG re-encode of a 1568x554 viewport, NOT the original PNG. Fidelity limit is deliberate: writing the source PNG to disk would be a file download, which needs the user's explicit permission and was not requested. Full-resolution pixels remain retrievable from source_image_url.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) - MP40

cards.element: one frame of the MP40 reload animation, first person, cut out to alpha
cards.evidence_tier: 2 - shipped game art, but community-extracted rather than a first-party or self-taken capture. The transparent background proves an editor processed it.
cards.visual_description: MP40 seen from its left side, canted steeply muzzle-up-left with the receiver running down to the lower right; front sight ring at top-left, rear sight leaf and charging-handle knob visible along the receiver. A separate dark angular slab sits at the lower-left, clearly detached from the weapon with background visible in the gap between them, clipped by the left and bottom frame edges - the magazine, out of the gun and falling away. The weapon's magazine housing carries no magazine.

measurement.method: Connected-component labelling on the PNG alpha channel (threshold a>40, 4-connectivity), run in-page over a 661x368 canvas.
measurement.result: Exactly 2 components. Weapon = 84614 px, bbox (39,0)-(659,367). Detached object = 3717 px, bbox (0,276)-(80,367), 81x92 px. No opaque path connects them.
measurement.why_it_matters: This is what makes 'the magazine visibly leaves the weapon' an objective finding rather than my reading of a small dark shape. The separation is topological, not judged by eye.

cards.answers: competitive-analysis question 1, first half: YES, the magazine visibly and completely leaves the weapon in BO1's MP40 reload.
cards.does_not_answer: The second half - one arc or two beats (mag-out then mag-in). A single frame cannot establish the beat structure of an animation. That remains an open gap; only motion evidence settles it.
cards.provenance: Single wiki file from a single uploader. ONE data point, uncorroborated - no second independent capture of this animation was obtained.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) - MP40

cards.element: MP40 aim-down-sights view, cut out to alpha and cropped
cards.evidence_tier: 3 - shipped game art, community-extracted AND cropped. The crop is what costs it a tier: it destroys the frame reference the question needs.
cards.visual_description: Rear view down the MP40's receiver. The rear sight leaf stands proud at the top with a squared notch, and the hooded front sight post sits centred inside that notch - a conventional aligned iron-sight picture. The receiver fills the lower centre; the bolt handle is a small stub on the left. Background is fully transparent: no HUD, no crosshair, no environment, and no frame edges belonging to the game.
cards.answers: Partially, competitive-analysis question 3: BO1's MP40 ADS is a TRUE iron-sight alignment - front post centred in the rear notch, weapon rolled upright, barrel level. It is a hard sight picture, not a lowered 'gun sits below the line' pose.
cards.does_not_answer: The actual number asked for. Measuring how far the weapon's top plane sits under the view axis requires the crosshair or the game's frame centre as a datum, and this image has NEITHER - it is cut out and cropped, so the weapon is not even centred within the file. Do NOT measure our '1 art unit of clear air' against this image; it cannot carry that comparison. [CORRECTED 2026-08-02: this field previously read 'sight column sits at about 0.70 of file width', which was never measured and is wrong. Measured by scholar-core on the stored JPEG, background-keyed against the flat page fill (PIL): subject spans x 324->666 of 1568, i.e. 0.207->0.425 of width, centre 0.316 - offset LEFT of centre, not right. The conclusion above is unaffected: the image lacks a crosshair or frame datum, so it cannot carry the measurement either way.]
cards.provenance: Single wiki file, one uploader. ONE data point.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) - MP40

cards.element: MP40 first-person viewmodel with the player's supporting hand in frame
cards.evidence_tier: 3 - shipped game art, community-extracted and cropped; pose is not confirmed to be the idle/hip rest specifically.
cards.visual_description: MP40 from the left rear, canted muzzle-up-left, running diagonally out of the lower-left of frame. The player's left hand and forearm are visible gripping under the receiver at the left edge, skin clearly rendered. The receiver carries stencilled 'MP40' lettering with scratched handwritten graffiti beneath it. Front sight ring and rear sight are both visible along the top. Background fully transparent.
cards.answers: That BO1's viewmodel puts a visible supporting HAND in frame on the weapon, and that the zombies-era MP40 carries hand-scrawled graffiti on the receiver - a texture-level detail, not a geometry one.
cards.does_not_answer: Whether this is the hip rest pose. The cut-out and crop remove the frame, so screen-height occupancy and cant angle relative to the view axis are NOT measurable from it. Treat the pose label as unconfirmed.
cards.provenance: Single wiki file, one uploader. ONE data point.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) - M1911

cards.element: one frame of the M1911 reload animation, first person, cut out to alpha
cards.evidence_tier: 2 - shipped game art, community-extracted. Transparent background proves an editor processed it.
cards.visual_description: M1911 held high and canted muzzle-up-left, gripped in a black-gloved right hand. Rear sight, slide serrations and the frame left flank are all readable. Below and left of the grip a SECOND flat object rises toward the magwell: a plate carrying a row of round dimples along its face, separated from the checkered grip panel by a lit edge. Both gloved hands are in frame, one on the grip and one under the second object.

measurement.method: Connected-component labelling on the PNG alpha channel (threshold a>40, 4-connectivity), run in-page over a 640x538 canvas - the SAME method as the MP40 card.
measurement.result: Background IS alpha-transparent (modal border sample rgba 0,0,0,0 over 75.7% of the border ring). Foreground = 139,913 px. Exactly 3 components, but the largest is 139,900 px with bbox (14,31)-(615,537) - ONE component covers 99.99% of the foreground. The other two total 13 px.
measurement.why_it_matters: NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is the important one. The test cannot separate a detached magazine here because the two HANDS bridge the weapon and the magazine into one opaque blob. That means the MP40 card's clean 2-component split is a consequence of the SAME property competitive-analysis used to attack it - that frame has no hands. The MP40 topological result and the no-hands objection are therefore NOT independent, and the topology adds no confirmation the objection does not already remove.

cards.answers: That BO1's M1911 reload does put BOTH hands in frame with a second magazine-shaped object approaching the magwell - so this wiki does keep hands for this weapon's reload, and a hands-free MP40 frame is anomalous for the same wiki.
cards.does_not_answer: Whether the magazine is fully clear of the weapon. That is an EYE JUDGEMENT here (medium confidence), not a measurement - the alpha topology is inapplicable, see measurement.why_it_matters. Also does not answer beat structure.
cards.provenance: Single wiki file, one uploader. ONE data point, independent of the MP40 file only in the weak sense of being a different upload on the same wiki.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) Zombies - RPK

cards.element: RPK first-person viewmodel, in-game screenshot WITH the HUD and the game frame intact
cards.evidence_tier: 2 - an uncropped in-game screenshot, NOT a cut-out. Better tier than every MP40 card in this corpus: frame edges, crosshair and HUD are all present, so screen-fraction and pose ARE measurable from it, unlike the alpha cut-outs.
cards.visual_description: 960x640 gameplay frame, wood-and-plaster interior, points 1950, ammo 100/400. The RPK occupies the lower right of the frame with the muzzle running AWAY and to the LEFT: wooden handguard and front sight at the weapon's upper left, receiver running down to the lower right, folded bipod under the barrel, and a large dark rectangular mass at the extreme right that is the drum/stock group. The flank turned toward the camera is a broad, essentially featureless expanse - no charging handle, no reciprocating part and no ejection port is drawn on it. A knife blade is visible at bottom centre.
cards.answers: BOTH questions it was captured for. (1) BO1's own RPK viewmodel resolves the weapon's LEFT flank toward the camera with the muzzle yawed inward and away - the same convention gunart.gd's rest pose uses, now corroborated from the reference rather than inferred from our own art. (2) NO moving part is visible on that flank at rest: the visible side of BO1's RPK is as mechanically inert as ours.
cards.does_not_answer: What the fire animation does. A rest still cannot show whether viewmodel_rpk_fire animates anything, and cannot rule out a small motion the JPEG re-encode would lose. It also does not settle whether BO1 MIRRORED the handle onto the visible side - at this resolution a mirrored knob and a bare receiver are not distinguishable.
cards.provenance: Single wiki file, one uploader. Corroborated on the specific point 'far-side mechanism gets no idle treatment' by an INDEPENDENT source: BO1's own rpk_zm weapon file leaves emptyIdleAnim blank, one of only two weapons on the 14-row roster that does.

source.product: Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010) - RPK

cards.element: one frame of the RPK cocking/charging animation, first person, cut out to alpha
cards.evidence_tier: 3 - shipped game art, community-extracted AND cropped, and the file NAME is the only thing asserting which action this is. Bare forearms date it to a Vietnam-era singleplayer level, not Zombies.
cards.visual_description: The weapon is canted FAR from any rest pose: muzzle up and to the LEFT at roughly 45 degrees or more, receiver running down to the lower right, wooden handguard and leather sling clearly readable, bipod at the lower left. A bare (ungloved) forearm and hand fill the right third of the frame very close to camera, crossed over toward the receiver.
cards.answers: The idiom, which is the transferable part: when BO1 needs the player to read a mechanical action, it RE-POSES THE WHOLE WEAPON - a large rotation plus a translation, far larger than the moving part's own travel - rather than relying on the part's motion inside the rest pose. The same is visible in M1911_Cocking_BO.png, where the pistol is rolled so the top of the slide faces the camera and the support hand comes over the top.
cards.does_not_answer: WHICH part is being worked, and whether the charging handle is drawn on the near flank. The resolution and the crop do not support that read. Do not cite this image for anything about the handle itself.
cards.provenance: Single wiki file, one uploader. The 're-pose for a mechanical action' reading is corroborated by a second independent file (M1911_Cocking_BO.png) showing the same idiom on a different weapon.

gaps.question: Is BO1's reload one arc or two distinct beats (mag-out, then mag-in)?
gaps.reason: Beat structure is a motion fact. No animated source was obtainable: YouTube video playback is hard-blocked in this browser (see blocked_sources), and a Fandom API sweep of all 84 files with the MP40 prefix returned ZERO .gif assets, so the wiki holds no animated reference either.
gaps.not_the_reason: NOT a browser-permission gap. The browser tier works; this was verified by capturing three images through it.

gaps.question: Is a casing visible in the viewmodel frame at typical framing, and does it arc right-and-back?
gaps.status: OPEN - no capture attempted to completion
gaps.reason: Same motion-evidence problem, and worse: a casing is airborne for a few frames, so even a lucky still is unlikely to catch one. Ruled not obtainable from still wiki assets within budget. The pattern directory was REMOVED rather than left empty, because an empty directory is invisible to git and reads as coverage.

gaps.question: Does BO1 MIRROR a far-flank control (AK/RPK charging handle) onto the viewmodel's visible left side, the way FPP weapon-art practice describes doing for sight knobs?
gaps.reason: Both RPK stills obtained are too low-resolution and too heavily cropped/canted to resolve a knob on the near flank. Settling it needs either a viewmodel-model rip or a high-resolution near-flank still, neither obtainable from wiki assets.
gaps.not_the_reason: NOT a browser block. Three further images were captured through the browser tier in the same session.

blocked_sources.evidence: On a reloaded watch page with network tracking active: ZERO requests to googlevideo.com (the media host is never contacted), while every youtube.com API call returned 503 (/youtubei/v1/log_event x3, /generate_204 x3, /api/stats/qoe). Static CDNs were healthy in the same capture: i.ytimg.com 200, yt3.ggpht.com 200, fonts.gstatic.com 200. Player API reported getPlayerState()==3 (buffering) across 20 consecutive 1s polls while video.readyState stayed 0, videoWidth 0, duration null - though getDuration() correctly returned 4s from metadata.
blocked_sources.ruled_out: Not a wedged player, not quality negotiation, not the specific clip: playback quality was forced to medium and playVideo() was called explicitly, with no change.
blocked_sources.consequence: Every motion-dependent visual question in this package is unanswerable from this environment until the video path is unblocked.
